title: SLO & Capacity Fallback Rehearsal - Release Prep
summary: Tabletop-style rehearsal to validate SLO fallback policies, surge capacity behavior, and gaps in the runbook ahead of the private deployment beta. Focus on routing fallbacks, KV-cache warmup, and telemetry gaps. Action items assigned for simulated traffic runner, runbook edits, and canary dashboard templates.
topics: model fallback routing and variant compatibility
action_items: Liam Chen|Create a synthetic traffic generator to emulate slow tail-latency + high qps; add to ci/smoke; ticket #INF-893|2026-05-27
Priya Gupta|Expand model-compatibility matrix for fallback variants (quantized vs fp16) and publish to ops-confluence|2026-05-25
Samira Khan|Add verification tests for KV-cache hit-rate on cold starts; integrate with nightly job|2026-05-28
Diego Ramos|Provision a 24h burst pool and document autoscale trigger thresholds|2026-05-24
Jenn Park|Draft short customer-facing note about fallbacks and expected behavior for beta customers|2026-05-29
next_steps: Run the synthetic traffic job in staging this week and capture SLO burn charts
Priya to update the compatibility matrix and notify teams
Schedule a focused SRE/Runtime follow-up to implement KV warmup hooks
Ship runbook PR and get sign-off from oncall lead
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 78m | Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Diego, Jenn, Alexei, Samira
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (PM): okay everyone, thanks for joining the SLO and capacity rehearsal. we have 78 minutes roughly. goal is to run two tabletop scenarios and identify any runbook gaps, especially around fallback routing and cache warmup.
[00:17] Liam (SRE): cool, i'll kick off with scenario A — a sudden 4x qps spike with increasing 95th pct latency and partial model OOMs on the older fp32 pool. assume dedicated pool is at 80% before spike.
[00:34] Priya (Eng Lead): quick clar — are we simulating KV-cache cold start too? that was a big contributor last time.
[00:42] Liam: yes, add cold cache and long-tail seq lengths, like a mix of 128-2048 tokens; this will hit kv cash, sorry, kv cache, heavily.
[00:55] Alexei (Runtime): note — our current fallback plan routes to quantized variants if latency SLOs are breached, but some callers use operators that expect fp16 behavior, so we need the compatibility matrix.
[01:12] Jenn (Product): customers will want a clear explanation: will output change? what do we promise on semantic parity when we fallback?
[01:23] Diego (Infra): also remember region fallback, network egress can add 40-80ms if we move across zones. that can break our 200ms p50 target.
[01:36] Samira (QA): i'll be watching for flakiness in the canary asserts — last run had spurious failures when the canary couldn't authenticate to the private-control-plane.
[01:50] Maya: ok scenario steps — Liam, run the spike; Alexei and Priya observe kernel selection and model variant swap; Diego watches autoscaler and burst pool allocations; Samira validates test stability. we'll pause at key decision points.
[02:11] [soft chatter / typing noises]
[02:28] Liam: starting synthetic spike now — running workload generator with 4x base qps, adding long sequences and a 10% request path that touches our largest model.
[02:45] Liam: staging dashboards are up — oh, p95 is climbing, and we see queue buildup on the GPU worker pool.
[03:01] Alexei: runtime's continuous batching is backpressure-ing, some requests are getting queued; kernel fallback to the smaller block kernels is happening. but i see increased GPU mem fragmentation.
[03:18] Priya: are there any OOM kills?
[03:22] Liam: a couple of small containers restarted — not full node OOM, but process restarts.
[03:31] Maya: decision point — do we trigger fallback routing to quantized variants now or scale out? discuss tradeoffs.
[03:41] Diego: if we scale another node, cold start time for the worker will be ~60s and KV-cache will be cold which will spike latency further; fallback reduces latency immediately but may affect output fidelity.
[03:56] Alexei: also note, our routing policy currently tries region-first then model-variant. maybe switch to 'variant-first' when throughput crosses X.
[04:05] Priya: variant-first makes sense for latency SLOs, but for regulated customers we have to respect pinned versions — need per-tenant policy exceptions.
[04:19] Jenn: can we communicate pinned-tenant behavior in the UI so customers know why their requests didn't fallback? otherwise they will raise support tickets.
[04:28] Maya: action — Priya to expand matrix + tenancy exceptions; Jenn to draft the UI/UX note.
[04:36] [08:00] Liam: after toggling routing to variant-first we saw p95 drop by ~120ms within 2 minutes; however we also saw semantic drift on the test prompt for one quantized variant — the paraphrase score dropped slightly.
[08:24] Samira: that's expected; tests flagged small regressions — QA severity low but needs acceptance criteria.
[08:38] Maya: okay note that down; we need an eval threshold where we accept a small fidelity delta for latency gains. set by product.
[08:48] Jenn: propose a banded threshold: <5% BLEU/paraphrase drop acceptable for non-critical flows. anything above needs canary gating and explicit customer opt-in.
[09:00] Priya: moving on — scenario B: partial control plane latency spike and region failover. imagine the private control plane in us-west becomes intermittently slow; routing starts failing and fallback to hosted region happens.
[09:19] Diego: in that case we rely on cached tokens and local routing tables; if the control plane is slow, some autoscale decisions may be delayed — risk is that we end up overloading the local pool before we can failover.
[09:33] Alexei: runtime has a grace-mode where it will keep older kernels running and refuse new heavy inits for X seconds. we should exercise that.
[09:44] Liam: firing the control plane latency emulation — adding 300-500ms API latency to control plane responses.
[10:02] [noise, brief cross-talk]
[10:18] Samira: tests show oncall notebook couldn't fetch traces for 2 minutes; our alerting didn't tie that to the control plane latency metric. that's a runbook gap.
[10:33] Maya: action item: tie the 'tracing ingestion lag' metric to control-plane-alert correlation. Samira to add epic.
[10:44] Priya: technical detail — when we failover region, certain feature flags (like prefix-caching heuristics) are disabled for safety; we need a flag-synchronization step. currently it's manual.
[10:59] Diego: if it's manual, ops will be slow, causing further SLO breaches. we need automation for critical flags.
[11:11] Alexei: we can add a safe-sync job that runs on failover path — small change but needs testing.
[11:24] Priya: add to backlog and mark P0 for private beta.
[11:34] [silence for 20s]
[12:00] Maya: quick sanity check — do we have dashboards for expected vs observed token cost during fallback? finance asked for this.
[12:12] Jenn: not a complete view; we have token-level breakdown but not an aggregated forecast for fallback scenarios. that'll be useful for sales and product.
[12:23] Liam: i can extend the cost telemetry to surface projected cost delta when variant-first is active.
[12:34] Maya: great — include that in the synthetic run output.
[12:40] Samira: note on kv-cache warmup: we saw in the simulation that kv-hit rate took ~7 minutes to stabilize after a new worker came up; during that time latency was 30% higher for cache-miss-heavy requests.
[12:56] Alexei: runtime improvements: we could pre-warm KV keys for pinned models used in the canary traffic. but need a hook from CI to know which keys.
[13:08] Priya: or use a 'prefix-warm' config per model that the autoscaler triggers at scale-up.
[13:16] Diego: will need IAM perms and KMS token rotation considered; on private deployments the warmup agent will need network access to model artifact stores which is sometimes locked down.
[13:29] Maya: another runbook gap: the warmup flow and its permissions. action: Diego to draft the secure warmup flow and checklist.
[13:40] [background laptop pinging noises]
[14:00] Jenn: customer comms point — how do we phrase this when we tell beta customers? "We will fallback to lower-latency variants; you may notice small behavior changes. there's an opt-out if you require parity." keep it short.
[14:22] Priya: also include an observability link with the canary dashboard so they can see when fallback triggers.
[14:33] Maya: we'll put that in the beta onboarding doc. Jenn, please coordinate with CSM.
[14:42] Jenn: yes.
[15:00] [28:00] Scenario wrap-up discussion:
[28:12] Maya: overall notes — variant-first routing helps SLO but increases drift; need eval thresholds, expanded compatibility matrix, and a customer opt-out. KV-warmup needs automation and a documented secure flow; dashboards need cost delta and canary links.
[28:35] Priya: runtime fixes — we surfaced kernel fallback fragmentation; Alexei to investigate fragmentation mitigation and defragmentation heuristics.
[28:48] Alexei: i'll prototype a lightweight defrag pass and test on staging.
[28:56] Samira: QA will add stress tests for queue buildup and auth failure modes.
[29:05] Liam: i'll run the synthetic workload daily for a week and capture SLO burn; will push results to the ops channel.
[29:15] Diego: autoscale tuning — current scale-up threshold is 70% GPU util with cooldown 120s; propose reducing to 60% and cooldown 90s for beta. but that increases cost.
[29:29] Jenn: product trade — lower latency vs cost. we'll make this a toggle per deployment tier.
[29:38] Maya: agree. put as optional setting per cluster.
[29:46] [45:00] Quick open-floor Q&A:
[45:12] Engineer (unclear): can we metricize 'semantic drift' more concretely? paraphrase score, entailment delta?
[45:25] Samira: we already have a micro-eval runner, but need to make it a gating metric on canary switch.
[45:36] Priya: the gating should be fast — perhaps sample 200 queries from regen set and compute paraphrase distribution.
[45:48] Alexei: note that collecting samples in live traffic has privacy/PII considerations. keep eval inputs synthetic.
[45:58] Maya: good call.
[46:08] Diego: ops note — when region failover happened last retro, logs lost trace-id continuity; we need a cross-region trace-id aggregator or a mapping table.
[46:18] Liam: that's a new infra ticket.
[46:24] Maya: add that to action items.
[46:30] [60:00] Final recap and owners:
[60:12] Maya: readout: Liam — synthetic runner (due 5/27); Priya — compatibility matrix (5/25); Alexei — defrag prototype (no later than 6/3); Diego — warmup secure flow + autoscale proposal (5/24); Samira — kv cold-start tests + tracing correlation (5/28); Jenn — customer comms + dashboard links (5/29).
[60:40] Maya: any objections? silence. okay we'll proceed.
[60:50] Jenn: i'll start the beta note draft after this call.
[61:00] Priya: can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review synthetic-run output?
[61:07] Maya: yes i'll send a calendar invite.
[61:12] [closing chatter]
[61:30] Maya: thanks everyone — appreciated. end of rehearsal.
[61:40] [meeting ended]
questions: What is the acceptable semantic drift threshold when using quantized fallbacks?
How aggressive should autoscale be for private beta given cost tradeoffs?
Who owns flag synchronization during region failover?
